flags.quote: The position stays even, but moving your g1-knight to f3 leaves your pawn hanging to the black f6-knight. A better move would have been moving your b1-knight to c3 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Nf3 defends e4. The pawn is not hanging. The real idea is the fork trick: Nxe4, and if Nxe4 then d5 forks bishop and knight. Nc3 does not save the pawn either — the same trick still works. If you want to actually hold e4, say d3.

flags.quote: Moving your b8-knight to c6 is playable, but taking the pawn on e4 with your f6-knight would be better because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Undefended is a lie. The knight on f3 defends e4. Nxe4 is better because of the d5 fork after a recapture, not because the pawn is free. And the reason tag is saves_piece, which is nonsense for a pawn grab.

flags.quote: Moving your f6-knight to e8 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: I just retreated a developed knight to the back rank and you shrugged. This is the plan: clear f6 so I can play f5. If you cannot name a retreat's point, do not call it strongest.

flags.quote: Moving your king to h8 is the strongest move because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: Kh8 then Kh7 is a shuffle so I can push f5 without sitting on the a2-g8 diagonal. The king is not suddenly safer in the corner. You taught king safety for a waiting move.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f5 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: This is the pawn break I spent Ne8 and two king moves preparing. Center control is the same sentence you used on e4 and Nf6. Teach the break: open the f-file, hit e4, play toward the king.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on f5 with your c8-bishop is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: I recaptured the pawn White just took. That is restoring material, not winning an undefended pawn. wins_material on a recapture trains me to think every capture is a gift.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e7 with your d5-knight is the strongest move because you fork the black c6-knight and the black f5-bishop.
flags.critique: You traded a knight for a bishop. The knight on e7 is hanging and I recapture on the next ply. A fork that gets taken back immediately is an exchange, not a tactic I can bank. Say you swapped N for B and maybe picked up the bishop pair.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: g4 hits my bishop on f5. That is the whole move. The reason sitting on this ply is pawn_shield, which is the opposite of pushing the g-pawn in front of a castled king.

flags.quote: The position stays even, but taking the pawn on g4 with your bishop puts it where the white pawn can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been moving your bishop to e6 because it saves your bishop from capture.
flags.critique: hxg4 takes a bishop, not a knight. You mapped a 300-centipawn SEE bucket to the wrong piece name. Be6 as a retreat is fine. Do not make me scan the board for a knight that is not dying.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on f3 with your f8-rook is the strongest move because the knight was undefended and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: That sentence is broken. g4 left Nf3 without its pawn defender; I took a hanging knight. The 'pin' of the f2 pawn to the rook behind it is trivia — that pawn cannot step off the file anyway. Glue the clauses together or drop the pin.

flags.quote: Moving your king to g2 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The king walks up to attack the rook on f3. That is a one-sentence lesson. Instead I get strongest-move with king_more_exposed in the reasons, which is the opposite of why the move is good.

flags.quote: Moving your f3-rook to f8 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: Kg2 was eating my rook. I ran it home. saves_piece is the actual reason and you buried it under another phantom pin. Tell me the rook was hanging to the king.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to f6 is a mistake, but moving your queen to d7 would be better.
flags.critique: A 146-centipawn mistake with empty reasons and no because. Why is Qf6 bad? Why Qd7? This is a SAN swap, not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your h1-rook to h2 is a blunder, but moving your h1-rook to h3 would be better.
flags.critique: This is the game. Rh2 leaves f3 so Qf3+ forks king and bishop. Rh3 covers f3. You had a 485-centipawn blunder and a pin tag and you named neither the check nor the fork square.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-rook to f6 is a blunder, but moving your pawn to d5 would be better because you can likely take a bishop.
flags.critique: 'Likely take a bishop' is a hedged capture I cannot play unless White leaves Bc4. d5 attacks the bishop; say that. And you never said why Rf6 is a blunder: it dumps the rook onto the square g5 hits.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g5 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: g5 hits the rook that just blundered onto f6. That is the punishment. Queen-takes-g4 is a footnote. Do not lead with saves_piece when you are kicking a rook.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on h6 with your g-pawn is a mistake because the pawn was undefended. A better move would have been moving your c4-bishop to e6.
flags.critique: Taking a hanging pawn cannot be the reason the capture is a mistake. That because-clause is the wins_material template glued onto a bad capture. Be6 is the crush; explain why grabbing h6 is poisoned, not that the pawn was free.

flags.quote: Moving your c4-bishop to e6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Two plies ago you said Be6 was the improvement. Now it lands and you have nothing: no attack on the rook, no cramp, no queen-and-bishop battery. Empty strongest-move on the move you already wanted is lazy.

flags.quote: Moving your f5-rook to f6 is a blunder, but moving your f5-rook to f8 would be better.
flags.critique: Be6 is staring at my rook on f5. You did not say the rook is hanging. Rf8 versus Rf6 with no threat named is another SAN swap on a 340-centipawn blunder.

flags.quote: Moving your h2-rook to h3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Rook to h3 attacks my queen on f3. ignored_threat as the reason on a best move is a polarity bug. Hit the queen; do not shrug.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but taking the rook on h3 with your queen puts it at risk of attack from the white e6-bishop. A better move would have been taking the bishop on e3 with your queen because you fork the white h3-rook and the white queen and you take the defender of the white queen.
flags.critique: The bishop just takes the queen. 'At risk of attack' is soft when it is a recapture. Qxe3 forking rook and queen is the real lesson, then you wreck it with 'take the defender of the white queen.' Pick one idea and finish the sentence.

flags.quote: Moving your c6-knight to d4 is a mistake, but moving your f6-rook to f8 would be better because you pin the pawn to the king.
flags.critique: Nd4 hangs the knight to Be3. Teach hanging pieces. 'Pin the pawn to the king' never says which pawn or why walking into Bxd4 is worse than that pin.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your e3-bishop is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: The knight was hanging. I took it. Lead with hanging, not another unnamed pawn pin. I am tired of pin-the-pawn as the default because-clause.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Eval jumps from +807 to +2367 against me and you call it strongest. That is a 15-pawn swing labeled best because the played UCI matched the engine pick. If the eval dump says I just died, do not congratulate the corpse.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to g5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Queen raids toward my king on h7 and you give me a blank strongest-move. Also 1408 centipawns of 'loss' still classified best. Name the attack: g6, h6, mate ideas. Empty copy on a queen entry is a joke.

suggestions.title: Do not say strongest when eval loss is huge
suggestions.detail: classifyPlayedMove forces best when UCI matches the engine pick, so d5 (+1560cp) and Qg5 (+1408cp) still render 'is the strongest move'. A 1200 believes the label. If lossCp is above the good threshold, keep the engine-best flag internally but pick excellent/good/noisy copy instead of the strongest-move template.

suggestions.title: Never emit a SAN-only blunder line
suggestions.detail: Qf6, Rh2, Rf6 (ply 44) are mistake/blunder with empty or useless reasons: 'X is a blunder, but Y would be better.' If selectBecauseReasons is empty, fall back to the suggested move's first tactic, a hanging piece after the played move, or the refutation punchline. A 1200 needs the threat named on the worst moments, not a move swap.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures winning material
suggestions.detail: Bxf5 and similar recaptures fire wins_material because capturedSeeCp >= 80, then copy says 'the pawn was undefended.' Gate wins_material on net new material, not on capturing a unit that just captured. Recapture should stay a plain capture reason. This is the same lie on every equal trade in the dump.

suggestions.title: Do not say undefended when the piece has defenders
suggestions.detail: Nf3 'leaves your pawn hanging' and Nxe4 'because the pawn was undefended' are SEE-positive captures on a defended e4. Copy hanging/undefended only when defender count is 0. If Nxe4 is good because ...d5 forks after the recapture, emit a follow-up fork/skewer reason from the PV, not hanging. A 1200 will count defenders and catch you.

suggestions.title: Do not explain a bad capture as a good capture
suggestions.detail: CONCEPT_PRIORITY lists capture before missed_improvement, so gxh6 (mistake, Lichess blunder) becomes 'a mistake because the pawn was undefended.' If classification is inaccuracy or worse, do not use capture/wins_material as playedBecause. Use the problem reason or the suggested move's benefit (Be6).

suggestions.title: Drop pins that cannot teach a move
suggestions.detail: Rxf3, Rf8, Bxd4, Nd4, Rh1 all lead with 'pin the pawn to the rook/king' without naming which pawn. Skip a pin if the pinned unit has no legal useful move along/off the line (file-pawns pinned to a rook behind them). Prefer hanging, capture, or attacks-queen when those exist. Pin spam is the most robotic because-clause in this game.

suggestions.title: Do not attach negative facts to best-move copy
suggestions.detail: Best moves here carry ignored_threat, king_more_exposed, pawn_shield, hanging. Kg2 attacks a rook while tagged king_more_exposed; g4 kicks a bishop while tagged pawn_shield; Rh3 hits a queen while tagged ignored_threat. Filter negative kinds out of because-selection when concept is best_move. Prefer kicked_by_pawn, checks, and attacks on a hanging enemy unit.

suggestions.title: Name the hanging piece, not a SEE bucket
suggestions.detail: Bxg4 says 'you lose a knight' because hangingLossCopy maps ~300cp to a knight while the piece on the square is a bishop. Use the hanging unit's type when the loss is that unit, and keep materialLabel only for net-exchange cases. Learners look for the named piece.

whatWorked: Nd5: 'strong outpost' is a real Italian lesson.
Qf3+: fork of king and bishop is the right tactic, named clearly.
Kingside castling copy (king tucks, rook comes in) is concrete.
d3 'saves your pawn from capture' is the first honest e4-protection line, even if plies 5–6 lied.
Re1 'open file' is short and true.
Bxh3 taking the hanging queen is the right recapture lesson.
